title: Sr. Staff Backend Engineer
Senior Software Engineer, Agentic AI
description_html:
<p><em>Clover is reinventing health insurance by working to keep people healthier.</em></p> <p>We value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. Healthcare is a universal concern, and we need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of healthcare. Clover's engineering team is empathetic, caring, and supportive. We are deliberate about the team and culture we are building. We seek engineers who are strong in their own work and care deeply about supporting each other's growth.</p> <p>We are looking for a senior software engineer to make Counterpart Health's existing customer-facing platform agentic. You will build applied AI systems that retrieve relevant information, call tools, and help healthcare users complete meaningful work. You will work with engineers, data scientists, and healthcare professionals, with ownership across data pipelines, backend services, model behavior, and the user experience.</p> <p><strong>As a Senior Software Engineer, you will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Simplify the complexities of healthcare by building systems that multiply human efforts.</li> <li>Build and maintain customer-facing agentic AI software, with ownership from data ingestion through to the user interface.<ul> <li>Develop retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, pipelines for ingestion, ETL, storage, indexing, retrieval, and context assembly.</li> <li>Build agent workflows that call tools and use application services, with clear permissions, execution limits, and human review where needed.</li> <li>Choose models, storage, retrieval, and orchestration patterns based on product needs and measured results.</li> </ul></li> <li>Protect PHI and tenant boundaries across data, prompts, retrieval, tools, and outputs in a HIPAA-regulated environment.</li> <li>Use customer feedback and failure analysis to improve answers and tool execution.</li> <li>Measure and improve quality, reliability, latency, and cost.</li> <li>Master new tools and technologies to solve concrete user problems while keeping the system simple enough for the team to maintain and operate.</li> <li>Help the team define development practices that support fast iteration and quality, including tests and documentation of key implementations.</li> <li>Work with Product Managers and operational staff to choose useful workflows, define success, and deliver features to customers.</li> </ul> <p><strong>You should get in touch if:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have personally owned a production agentic system used by external customers. You can explain your contribution across ingestion, ETL, storage, retrieval, the tool-calling loop, inference, and UI integration.</li> <li>You have used evaluations to improve a live system. Can explain the test data, failure categories, release criteria, and limits of automated or LLM-as-judge scoring.</li> <li>You bring senior software engineering experience and can write, test, debug, and operate the application code behind an AI feature. Python and TypeScript or JavaScript experience are useful, as is comparable experience in another production language.</li> <li>You have experience with SQL, APIs, data pipelines, and cloud services such as GCP or AWS.</li> <li>You have handled practical LLM limitations, such as context-window limits, unsupported answers, retrieval failures, and incorrect tool calls.</li> <li>Experience with healthcare or another regulated industry is a plus. Experience with tools such as LangGraph, Langfuse, pgvector, or OpenSearch is useful, but we care more about your engineering decisions and production results than a particular framework. Using AI coding assistants, building demos, or shipping internal tools alone does not meet the production AI experience required for this role.</li> </ul> <p><strong>You will love this job if:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You are curious about how systems work and use pragmatic engineering to solve complicated problems. You test whether an AI approach improves the workflow and use simpler software when it is the better choice.</li> <li>You enjoy a collaborative environment where you help define priorities and own delivery. You bring clarity to ambiguity and change your view when new evidence calls for it.</li> <li>You take responsibility for what reaches customers. You investigate broken behavior, fix the cause, and improve the tests and evaluations that should catch it.</li> <li>You care about what good technology can do for people and want to work with healthcare professionals on tools they can trust.</li> </ul> <hr /> <p><strong>Benefits Overview</strong>:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Financial Well-Being</strong>: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.</li> <li><strong>Physical Well-Being</strong>: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive group medical coverage that include coverage for hospitalization, outpatient care, optical services, and dental benefits.</li> <li><strong>Mental Well-Being</strong>: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous annual leave policy. title: Senior Software Engineer II
Senior Software Engineer II
Staff Platform Engineer
description_html:
Headquarters: New York, New York; Miami, Florida; Remote (USA)

About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Platform

Our Platform organization’s purpose is to enable Gemini to scale effectively and empower our engineering teams to focus on building innovative financial products and experiences for individuals around the world. Platform builds a scalable and secure foundation that enables Engineering to develop, deploy, validate, and operate services in production; improve reliability; reduce repetitive operational work; and improve system efficiency through architectural improvements.

The Platform team builds products for engineers. We work directly with product, application engineering, data, and security teams to understand their needs, establish safe defaults, and provide standard workflows for building and operating services. We treat internal platforms as production software with users, service-level objectives, roadmaps, documentation, and feedback loops.

The Role: Staff Platform Engineer

You will provide technical leadership for the software and infrastructure that form Gemini’s internal engineering platform. This is a software engineering role grounded in deep production and infrastructure experience. You will build self-service systems, developer tools, and automation that improve the way teams create, deploy, scale, observe, and operate services.

You will shape platform strategy across cloud, networking, compute, storage, infrastructure automation, CI/CD, and the systems required to run highly available services in production. You will partner with engineering, security, data, and product leaders to turn broad operational needs into reliable platform products, establish clear technical direction, and drive adoption across teams.

You will make infrastructure programmable, secure, observable, and resilient; use SLOs and error budgets to guide tradeoffs; and continuously replace manual operational work with well-designed software. The role spans software, systems, and infrastructure engineering, with an emphasis on solving cross-functional problems and delivering measurable improvements to developer productivity and production reliability.

What success looks like in this role: Engineers can safely self-serve common workflows through documented, well-supported platform products. Platform capabilities are adopted because they reduce complexity and improve outcomes. Reliability, deployment safety, developer experience, and infrastructure efficiency improve measurably over time. Operational load grows more slowly than the number and scale of services supported by the team. Platform engineers remain close to production while spending the majority of their time on durable software and systems improvements.

Responsibilities:

  • Set technical direction for platform capabilities and contribute to a long-term plan for cloud, networking, infrastructure, delivery, and reliability engineering.
  • Lead architecture recommendations and technical engagements across the software development lifecycle, from early design through production operation.
  • Design, build, and maintain platform services, APIs, CLIs, controllers, workflows, and automation in languages such as Go, TypeScript, Python, or similar; own them through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and production operation.
  • Build self-service capabilities that let engineers provision environments, deploy services, manage infrastructure, and respond to operational conditions safely without relying on manual platform intervention.
  • Experience with build tooling such as Bazel or Buck2.
  • Create and evolve standard workflows for service development and delivery, including templates, libraries, deployment workflows, policy-as-code, and reusable platform building blocks.
  • Design and improve the cloud, compute, storage, identity, and infrastructure building blocks used by engineering teams.
  • Design and operate core network infrastructure across public clouds and regions, including routing, connectivity, traffic management, and security controls.
  • Operate and improve the compute, container, networking, and cloud infrastructure that supports critical services and new workloads, including distributed and AI-enabled systems where appropriate.
  • Improve the systems and workflows used to provision infrastructure, connect services, deliver changes, and recover from failures across environments.
  • Define and use service-level indicators, SLOs, error budgets, and production-readiness standards with engineering teams to make reliability and launch decisions explicit and measurable.
  • Improve observability, alerting, capacity planning, performance, and failure handling; design systems that degrade gracefully, roll out progressively, and recover automatically where safe.
  • Lead or coordinate response to significant incidents, ensure effective post-incident follow-through, and turn recurring operational work into permanent improvements through postmortems.
  • Reduce repetitive operational work. Measure it, automate or eliminate it, and keep the team focused primarily on engineering work that improves reliability, scale, security, cost, or developer experience.
  • Influence engineering standards and practices across teams through design reviews, technical writing, prototypes, internal education, and direct collaboration.
  • Build alignment across competing priorities and stakeholders; make pragmatic tradeoffs while preserving clear interfaces and room for future evolution.
  • Mentor engineers, develop technical leaders, and raise the quality of platform engineering practices across Gemini.

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering, infrastructure engineering, SRE, or an equivalent combination of experience, including substantial ownership of production systems.
  • Strong software engineering ability in at least one language such as Go, Python, TypeScript, Rust, or similar, with experience building maintainable services, automation, CLIs, APIs, or developer tools.
  • Demonstrated experience operating infrastructure and distributed systems in production, including diagnosing failures, managing capacity, improving performance, and designing for high availability and recovery.
  • Experience designing, operating, or improving production systems across cloud infrastructure, networking, compute, storage, deployment platforms, or related infrastructure domains.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure and infrastructure as code, such as Terraform or an equivalent system.
  • Experience with containers and orchestration, such as Kubernetes, EKS, GKE, AKS, Docker, or Nomad, including workload deployment, networking, security, and operational troubleshooting.
  • Experience owning and managing cloud network security controls, including network firewalls, DNS filtering, and network segmentation.
  • Experience designing or improving CI/CD and automated software delivery systems, including testing, deployment, progressive rollout, rollback, and change validation.
  • Practical experience with observability: metrics, logs, traces, alerting, dashboards, and production health models. Familiarity with OpenTelemetry or comparable tooling is valuable.
  • Working knowledge of SLOs, error budgets, incident response, blameless postmortems, and techniques for reducing operational toil.
  • Experience with high-availability architectures, capacity planning, failure recovery, and the operational tradeoffs required to run critical systems at scale.
  • Experience building secure-by-default systems and collaborating with security teams on identity, access control, secrets, supply-chain security, and policy enforcement.
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar technologies and domains quickly, including the infrastructure and reliability characteristics of data-intensive, event-driven, or AI/ML workloads.
  • Track record of setting technical direction, leading architecture across multiple teams, and influencing decisions without relying on direct authority.
  • Experience mentoring engineers, developing technical leaders, and communicating complex technical tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong technical communication and leadership skills; able to turn cross-functional problems into maintainable systems and delivered results.
It Pays to Work Here
 
The compensation & benefits package for this role includes:
  • Competitive starting pay
  • A discretionary annual bonus
  • Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant
  • Comprehensive health plans
  • 401K with company matching
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Flexible time off

Salary Range: The base salary range for this role is between $168,000 - $240,000 in the State of New York. This range is not inclusive of our discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Expectations may vary by location and role, so candidates are encouraged to connect with their recruiter to learn more about the specific policy for the role. Employees who do not live near one of our hubs are part of our remote workforce. All employees, however, are required to onboard in-person at one of our office locations.

At Gemini, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our products, and we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. Equal Opportunity is the Law, and Gemini is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. If you have a specific need that requires accommodation, please let a member of the People Team know.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Platform Engineering
description_html:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the role
 Crusoe is building the AI cloud: vertically integrated GPU infrastructure spanning energy, data centers and a fast-growing cloud platform. Behind every customer-facing service sits a shared foundation our engineering teams build on: streaming and event platforms, workflow orchestration, identity-aware access, infrastructure-as-code, certificates, the service catalog, cloud cost, and the ability to recover from disaster.

We're hiring a Staff Platform Engineer to own the design and delivery of key parts of that foundation. You'll lead the technical direction for our streaming, workflow and resilience systems, helping turn strong but independently run systems into a coherent, self-service, production-grade platform. You'll lead through design docs, RFCs, design reviews and hands-on work, and partner closely with the Senior Staff Platform Engineer and platform leadership on broader architecture decisions.



What you'll own

Streaming and event platform

 - Drive the design and rollout of the Crusoe Streaming Platform, bringing NATS/JetStream (hub-and-leaf topology from data center to cloud), WarpStream/Kafka and Pub/Sub under one managed model with clear placement guidance per use case.

 - Take Apache Flink (Flink Kubernetes Operator) from development to multi-environment production: observability, capacity planning, resource quotas, upgrade policy, on-call readiness and self-service pipeline provisioning.

Workflow orchestration

 - Lead the migration from self-hosted Temporal to Temporal Cloud, including environment and account separation and a namespace-per-team model with self-service provisioning.

Disaster recovery exercises

 - Build and run the DR exercise program for platform services: Flink, NATS/WarpStream, Temporal, Cloud SQL/AlloyDB and the GKE clusters that host them.

 - Define RTO/RPO per service with service owners and prove them through game days, tabletop exercises and controlled failure injection (zone loss, dependency outages, credential or certificate expiry, accidental deletion).

 - Make recovery repeatable with tested backup and restore for stateful systems, documented failover runbooks and automation that rebuilds environments from code.

 - Turn every exercise into tracked remediation and report DR readiness to engineering leadership.

Partner and contribute

 - Infrastructure as code: contribute to Terraform and Scalr standards for the core GCP projects, including secrets scoping, least privilege and safe change management.

 - Access and edge: work with Security and the platform team on Pomerium/Okta, Envoy and cert-manager reliability.

 - Service catalog (Port): keep dependency and ownership data accurate for the systems you own so it supports DR and incident response.

 - Cost: help identify and deliver cost and rightsizing improvements for the services you own.

Technical leadership

 - Write and drive design docs and RFCs for your domains, and make clear build-vs-buy recommendations.

 - Define SLOs, on-call expectations, runbooks and upgrade policy for the systems you own.

 - Mentor senior engineers and raise the bar on design and operational quality across SRE and platform teams.



What you bring

 - 8+ years in software, platform or infrastructure engineering, including experience leading technical direction for shared systems used by multiple teams.

 - Deep, hands-on production experience with distributed streaming and messaging (Kafka or Kafka-compatible systems, NATS/JetStream or Pulsar) and stream processing (Flink or similar): durability, back-pressure, delivery guarantees and capacity planning.

 - Strong Kubernetes experience (GKE and/or self-managed), with GitOps (ArgoCD), Helm and operators.

 - Solid Terraform experience, including state management and governance tooling (Scalr, Terraform Cloud, Atlantis or similar).

 - Working knowledge of GCP (or AWS), cloud networking and IAM/Workload Identity.

 - Experience running workflow orchestration (Temporal, Cadence or similar) or other stateful platform services in production.

 - Experience designing or running disaster recovery exercises: setting RTO/RPO, testing backup and restore, running game days and driving the resulting fixes.

 - Experience delivering cross-team migrations with minimal disruption.

 - Proficiency in at least one of Go, Python or Java, and comfort writing production code.

 - Clear written communication: you can write a design doc or RFC that gets a decision made.



Nice to have

 - Experience operating WarpStream, Confluent or other object-storage-backed Kafka

 - Temporal Cloud or multi-tenant namespace design

 - Chaos engineering tooling (Chaos Mesh, Litmus, Gremlin or similar) and multi-region failover design

 - Familiarity with identity-aware proxies, Envoy, TLS/PKI and DNS

 - Internal developer portals (Port, Backstage)

 - Hybrid data center and cloud architectures, especially GPU and HPC environments

 - Open-source contributions to Kubernetes, Envoy, Flink, NATS or Terraform providers



Benefits:

 - Industry competitive pay 

 - Restricted Stock Units in a fast growing, well-funded technology company

 - Health insurance package options including HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

 - Employer contributions to HSA accounts

 - Paid Parental Leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Teladoc

 - 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4% of salary

 - Generous paid time off and holiday schedule

 - Cell phone reimbursement

 - Tuition reimbursement

 - Subscription to the Calm app

 - MetLife Legal

 - Company paid commuter benefit; $300 per month


Compensation:
Compensation will be paid in the range of $215,000 – $260,000 + bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation will be determined by the applicant's education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.
